TIMEBOX · USABILITY REVIEW · 6 NOVEMBER 2026

Before and after

Twelve usability improvements across the web and Android apps, focused on finding controls, completing edits, recovering from errors and understanding planned work.

These are real captures from the audit and the updated branch, not mockups. Only the mobile board has a comparable viewport pair; its sample data also differs. Day captures use different viewport sizes, and Android captures show different Settings regions. Missing historical captures are explicitly identified below. Click a screenshot to open its full resolution.

Screenshot comparisons

01 · Mobile task board — U2, U12

Before: the board extended beyond the screen and filters occupied substantial space. After: status links expose every column, task sections use the available width, and filters open on demand.

Compare layout and navigation, not Task counts: the original capture was empty and the updated capture contains synthetic review data.

02 · Day controls — U1

Before: scrolling the Day moved its controls out of view. After: the date, Tracking, View and lane context remain available in a sticky toolbar.

Different viewport sizes and scroll states: this is behavioral evidence, not a pixel-for-pixel comparison. Browser tests additionally verify visible controls on desktop and preserved zoom positioning.

03 · Android Settings — U5, U8

Before: Settings switches lacked accessible names and connection setup did not offer the new validation/test flow. After: switches are named, credentials are masked, and Test connection confirms server access separately from saving settings.

The captures show different Settings regions. The original connection fields were not separately captured; accessible names and key masking are verified by device tests, not by the appearance of these screenshots alone.

04 · Additional evidence — navigation and recurrence

These are separate features, not a comparison pair. No matching after Settings screenshot or before recurring-conflict screenshot was preserved. Settings scroll reset passed browser testing. The recurring recovery action was exercised against the review API.

All twelve improvements

U1

Day controls stay within reach

Date, Tracking, View and lane labels remain visible while scrolling. Timeline positioning accounts for the toolbar; whole-day viewing remains available.

U2

A mobile board you can navigate

Full-width status sections replace the wide mobile board. Status links include counts; filters are collapsed until needed.

U3

Clearer saving and recovery

Editors communicate saving, saved, unsaved and failed states. Failed drafts remain available for retry; in-flight saves block dismissal.

U4

Create a first plan directly

The empty Day explains that Task Types are optional and offers Create first plan. A regression verifies creation with no types configured.

U5

Testable Android connection setup

Validate the server address, test the entered address and key without saving, and distinguish saved settings from successful access. Keys are masked with Show/Hide.

U6

Usable calendar conflict time entry

Native date/time pickers replace ISO-string editing on Android. Duration and zone are visible; repeated DST times offer Earlier/Later choices.

U7

Searchable calendar assignment

Search Task Types and Tasks. Project or series context distinguishes Tasks with the same title.

U8

Accessible dialogs and exits

Shared focus containment, focus return, background isolation and error handling for web editors. Android routine loading/error screens retain Close.

U9

Recovery before technical setup

Network errors use plain language and recovery actions. Google Calendar setup details sit inside a disclosure.

U10

Actionable recurring-plan conflicts

Use task/series terminology. Show the affected Task, occupied date/time and reason, with View day and an eligible explicit Add to Ready to Plan action.

U11

More predictable date entry

Time-first entry is retained. Invalid or incomplete dates block saving, date bounds match the picker, and scheduling identifies the Reporting Time Zone.

U12

Larger, named controls

Larger interaction areas for sidebar, filters, date controls, recurrence and close actions. Priority controls have group labels; Android’s existing 48 dp switch targets remain.

What was verified

  • Web: 478 tests in the full run; the additional first-plan regression subsequently passed in a 25/25 TodayPage run.
  • Browser: all 16 cases passed across the full run and focused rerun. Six affected keyboard, navigation and zoom cases passed again after final layout refinements.
  • Android: 467 JVM tests and 11 focused device tests passed, including key masking and routine loading/error exits.
  • Live review: recurring recovery confirmed Ready to Plan; Android connection testing confirmed server access; Today navigation used the shared reporting date.

Screenshots do not establish accessibility compliance. TalkBack speech, actual notifications, live Google OAuth/import, physical devices and exhaustive large-font/landscape layouts were not tested. The full Android instrumentation suite was not rerun; unrelated baseline failures remain documented.

Source: the Timebox audit and resolution records, 6 November 2026. Branch: t3/bug-usability-audit. All screenshots use local review data. Implementation was left unmerged for review. Expand each comparison to inspect its evidence.
